⚖️ MYTH vs FACT

❌ Myth: Every Slip Disc Requires Surgery

✅ Fact: Most patients improve without surgery.

A slip disc diagnosis can be worrying, but surgery is not the answer for everyone. In fact, most patients recover successfully with medications, physiotherapy, lifestyle modifications, and guided rehabilitation.

Surgery is generally reserved for selected situations such as persistent severe pain, progressive neurological weakness, or loss of bladder and bowel control.

The most important principle in spine care is to treat the patient's symptoms and clinical condition—not just the MRI report.

If you are experiencing back pain, leg pain, or have concerns about your MRI findings, a proper clinical evaluation can help determine the best treatment approach.

🩺 Dr. Siddharth Katkade
Consultant Spine Surgeon
Bombay Spine Clinic™

🦴 *SPINE TIP OF THE WEEK*

*THE 10-SECOND SCOLIOSIS CHECK*
*Could Your Child Have a Curved Spine?*

Many children with scoliosis have *no pain at all*, which is why it often goes unnoticed until the curve becomes more obvious.

The good news? A simple 10-second check at home can help identify early warning signs.

👀 *What to look for:*
✅ One shoulder higher than the other
✅ Uneven waistline
✅ One side of the rib cage appearing more prominent
✅ Leaning to one side while standing
✅ Uneven posture in photographs

💡 *Try this simple test:*
Ask your child to stand with feet together, bend forward, and touch their toes while you observe from behind.

Early detection can make a significant difference, especially during growth spurts between *10–16 years of age*.

Remember:
👉 Not every uneven shoulder means scoliosis.
👉 But if you notice any of these signs, it's worth getting the spine evaluated.

A quick 10-second check today could make a lifelong difference tomorrow.

📤 Please share this with parents, teachers, coaches, school groups, and anyone involved in children's health and development. Early awareness matters. 😊

🏃‍♂️ Spine Tip of the Week | The Runner's Paradox

Many runners have excellent cardiovascular fitness and endurance, but running alone may not fully protect against age-related muscle loss (sarcopenia), reduced strength, or declining bone health.

While running trains your heart, strength training helps protect your muscles, bones, joints, and spine.

Benefits of regular strength training for runners:
✅ Improved running efficiency
✅ Better spine support
✅ Reduced injury risk
✅ Stronger muscles and bones
✅ Prevention of age-related muscle loss

A simple goal: For every 3–4 running sessions per week, include at least 2 strength-training sessions. Even 20 minutes twice weekly can make a meaningful difference.

At Bombay Spine Clinic, we encourage runners and active individuals to focus on both endurance and strength for long-term spine health and injury prevention.

📍 Bombay Spine Clinic
Dr. Siddharth Katkade | Consultant Spine Surgeon

🦴 Spine Tip of the Week | Text Neck Syndrome

Do you spend several hours daily looking at your phone, laptop, or tablet?

Prolonged screen use can place excessive stress on the cervical spine, leading to a condition commonly known as **Text Neck Syndrome**. As the head tilts forward, the load on the neck muscles and cervical discs increases significantly, contributing to neck pain, shoulder stiffness, headaches, poor posture, and upper back discomfort.

A simple habit can help:
✅ Hold your phone closer to eye level
✅ Avoid prolonged neck flexion
✅ Take movement breaks every 20–30 minutes
✅ Perform gentle neck and upper back stretches regularly

At Bombay Spine Clinic, we frequently see patients with posture-related neck pain, cervical spondylosis, office-related neck strain, and screen-time-associated spine problems.

Early attention to posture and ergonomics can help reduce long-term stress on the spine and improve overall neck health.

📍 Bombay Spine Clinic
Dr. Siddharth Katkade | Consultant Spine Surgeon

🦴 Spine Tip of the Week | Healthy Hips, Strong Spine

Did you know tight hips and pelvic imbalance can contribute to lower back pain, poor posture, stiffness, and reduced spinal mobility?

Limited hip mobility forces the lower back to compensate, increasing stress on the lumbar spine over time. Simple hip mobility exercises and pelvic tilt movements can help improve posture, reduce back strain, and support a healthier spine.

✅ Improve posture
✅ Reduce lower back pain
✅ Increase flexibility & mobility
✅ Support spinal alignment

At Bombay Spine Clinic, we commonly see posture-related back pain, sitting-related spine issues, and hip-spine imbalance in office workers, gym-goers, and sedentary lifestyles.

🦴 Spine Tip of the Week | The 20-20-20 Eye–Neck Rule

Prolonged screen time and desk work can contribute to neck pain, upper back stiffness, eye strain, poor posture, and “tech neck syndrome.”

A simple evidence-based habit that helps:
✅ Every 20 minutes
✅ Look 20 feet away
✅ For 20 seconds

The 20-20-20 rule helps relax neck muscles, reduce screen fatigue, improve posture, and decrease strain on the cervical spine. Simple neck stretches during work breaks can further support spinal health and mobility.

At Bombay Spine Clinic, we commonly see patients with office-related neck pain, posture-related spine problems, cervical spondylosis, and work-from-home back pain linked to prolonged screen usage and poor ergonomics.

🩺 SPINE CLINICAL INSIGHT
Degenerative Cervical Myelopathy (DCM) is often missed in routine OPD practice and treated as simple cervical spondylosis.

Early clues include:
✔️ Hand clumsiness
✔️ Gait imbalance or frequent falls
✔️ Hoffmann’s positive sign
✔️ Progressive weakness or stiffness
✔️ Bilateral upper limb symptoms

🚨 Red Flags Requiring Urgent Referral:
* Bowel/bladder dysfunction
* Rapidly progressive weakness
* Severe gait instability

📌 MRI Cervical Spine remains the gold standard investigation.

Early diagnosis and timely referral can prevent irreversible neurological decline and improve patient outcomes.

🦴 Spine Health Reminder | Don’t Sit Too Long

Long hours of sitting can put extra stress on your spine, leading to back pain, neck stiffness, and posture problems. Poor sitting habits may also affect spinal discs and reduce flexibility over time.

💡 Healthy Spine Tip:
Take a short break every 30 minutes.
🚶 Walk a little
🧘 Stretch your body
🙆 Improve your posture

I don’t even know where to begin, because what Dr. Jeet Savla did for my mother and for us as a family means so much more than just a surgery.

I have known him from before, because he had operated on me, and that experience itself had built a lot of trust. I remember how calm and clear he was through everything, and that stayed with me. But this time, when it came to my mother, the situation was very different. It was emotional, stressful, and honestly very scary for us.

My mom’s finger condition had become really bad in our hometown. What initially felt like something small kept getting worse over time. There were delays, things didn’t improve, and at one point it reached a stage where just looking at her hand would make my heart sink. Seeing your parent in pain and not being able to fix it immediately is one of the most helpless feelings. As a family, we were anxious, confused, and mentally exhausted.

When we finally connected with Dr. Savla, the first thing he gave us was calm. He listened to everything patiently, understood how serious it had become, and explained what needed to be done. He never made us feel rushed or dismissed. He understood not just the medical side, but also what we were going through emotionally.

The surgery wasn’t simple, especially because of how much the condition had already progressed. But he handled it with so much focus and confidence that it gave us strength. I remember feeling a sense of relief just knowing he was the one taking care of her.

What stayed with me the most was that his care didn’t stop at the surgery. He stayed connected, kept checking on her recovery, and made sure she was healing properly. It never felt transactional. It felt like he genuinely cared.

Today, seeing my mother recover and slowly get back to her normal life feels like we’ve been given peace back. Those days of fear and uncertainty feel behind us, and a big reason for that is him.

For me, Dr. Jeet Savla will always be someone I trust deeply. Not just because he is a great surgeon, but because of the way he shows up for his patients and their families when they need it the most.

I will always be grateful to him for being there for my mother and for us during such a difficult time.

Many patients in Santacruz experience repeated neck pain affecting daily activities.

Neck pain that keeps returning is often a sign that the underlying cause needs attention. Many people experience temporary relief with rest or medication, but the discomfort may come back if factors affecting the neck are not addressed.

Common reasons for recurring neck pain include poor posture, prolonged screen time, muscle weakness, stress-related tension, previous neck injuries, cervical disc problems, or age-related changes in the spine. Spending long hours looking down at mobile devices or working without proper ergonomic support can place continuous strain on the neck muscles and joints.

Some people may notice stiffness, restricted neck movement, shoulder pain, headaches, or pain spreading toward the arms. In certain cases, symptoms like tingling, numbness, or weakness may indicate nerve irritation and require proper evaluation.

Managing recurring neck pain involves more than temporary pain relief. Improving posture, strengthening neck and upper back muscles, maintaining healthy movement habits, and following appropriate exercises can support long-term spine health.

A detailed spine assessment helps identify whether the pain is related to muscles, discs, nerves, or other cervical spine conditions. Understanding the actual cause is the first step toward effective management and preventing repeated discomfort.

Pott’s spine is a type of spinal infection that can affect the bones, discs, and surrounding tissues of the spine. Many patients are concerned whether this condition can cause leg weakness or numbness, especially when symptoms progress over time.

In the early stages, Pott’s spine may cause persistent back pain, stiffness, fatigue, or discomfort. However, if the infection leads to swelling, bone damage, or pressure on the spinal cord or nerves, it can result in nerve-related symptoms such as tingling, numbness, leg weakness, difficulty walking, or changes in balance.

The severity of nerve symptoms depends on the location of infection, the amount of spinal cord or nerve compression, and how early treatment is started. Not every patient with Pott’s spine develops weakness or numbness, but these symptoms should not be ignored.

Diagnosis usually involves a detailed clinical assessment, blood tests, and imaging such as MRI to understand the extent of infection and nerve involvement. This was despite us clearly stating that we wanted to do the test at another known place. He claimed that ultrasounds done elsewhere would not be reliable. The lab he suggested charged ₹6000, while we got the same test done at our known place for ₹5000.

As instructed, we shared the report with him on WhatsApp, but there was no response. Later, my brother personally visited the clinic just to show the reports (the patient was not present). Ideally, this should have been free since it was only for report discussion, but he still charged ₹1000. On top of that, he again recommended another radiologist by sharing a specific name and phone number.

Overall, this was the most money-minded and disappointing experience I’ve had with a doctor.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Hello! I really feel sorry for patients like you.It is unfortunate that when a correct clinical diagnosis was made and appropriate steps were taken to prevent you from being misled, the response is criticism rather than appreciation. You previously did an incorrect scan elsewhere, which you don't have anything to say about. Now, when a correct scan was suggested after clinical examination, and a correct diagnosis was made, here you are making allegations without even having visited for the follow up consultation and understanding the problem. Let's get the facts clear!

The reason a specific centre was suggested, was to prevent a repeat of an incorrect investigation (like you did before). Prior to consulting me, a venous Doppler had already been done, while your mother’s clinical presentation was not sciatica or venous problem, but strongly suggestive of arterial insufficiency (ischemic pain). A venous Doppler would never diagnose this condition.

The recommendation was therefore for a proper arterial Doppler, done by a senior, reliable radiologist, with whom precise requirements could be clearly communicated. The phone call was made only to ensure the correct study was performed this time — not for any financial reason. I have no commission arrangements, nor do I compel patients to visit any particular center. You were always free to choose where to do the test, which you ultimately did — and the scan confirmed the arterial block, exactly as suspected clinically. (which you should rather appreciate for spot on clinical diagnosis!)

Suggesting accuracy over repetition of wrong tests is called responsible medical practice, not “money-mindedness”.

At no point were you instructed to seek treatment or consultation over WhatsApp. Medical opinions are not given casually over messages.

Your brother later visited the clinic for formal report discussion and guidance, which constitutes a consultation. Doctors do not charge for “presence of the patient” — they charge for professional expertise, time, and responsibility involved in interpreting reports and guiding next steps. This is the same principle by which professionals in any field are paid for their work. Do you or your family members work for free? or ever say to your boss that you don't want payment for a particular month? or a 50% less salary this month would be okay?

If there was any financial difficulty, it could have been communicated. We offer concessions, fee waivers, and charity OPD options for genuinely needy patients. We doctors do that.

It is disappointing that sincere efforts to guide a patient onto the correct diagnostic path are interpreted otherwise. Medicine requires trust in clinical judgment, not assumptions about intent.

I genuinely wish your mother good health. However, when decision-makers are like you who lack trust and respect for sound medical advice, it may indeed be better to continue with whose approach you are more comfortable with and keep on doing investigation after investigations. All the best! 👍🏻

featured_reviews.name: VANITA CHOUDHARI
featured_reviews.review_text:
My family has had two remarkable experiences with Dr. Kunal Shah in Kadamwadi, and I felt it was important to share them.
First Experience
My mother-in-law suffered a fall on 3rd March. We called the clinic around 8:00 PM, and the receptionist was extremely helpful in arranging an immediate consultation with Dr. Kunal Shah.
The clinic has an in-house X-ray facility, which helped speed up the diagnosis. As soon as the X-rays were reviewed, Dr. Shah promptly made the necessary decisions regarding treatment. He was precise, confident, and acted without delay. A plaster was applied immediately, and despite it being late in the evening, the doctor and his staff stayed until around 10:30–10:45 PM to ensure everything was completed properly.
The required medicines were prescribed, and we were advised to follow up after a month. Dr. Shah had also performed my mother-in-law's back surgery. The surgery went smoothly, and she was able to start walking the very next day.
Dr. Kunal Shah is exceptionally focused, highly skilled, and one of the finest orthopedic surgeons I have come across. After witnessing the quality of treatment provided to my mother-in-law, I became confident in recommending him to family and friends without hesitation.

Second Experience
A month later, my brother met with an accident. At Gurunanak Hospital's casualty department, we were advised that he would require surgery because one of his ankle bones had broken into several pieces (where a metal plate will be fixed inside).
As soon as I learned about the situation, I contacted Dr. Kunal Shah's clinic and shared the X-rays that had been taken at Hospital. After reviewing them, Dr. Shah informed us that the fracture could potentially be treated without surgery.
I immediately brought my brother to Dr. Shah's clinic. Once again, the receptionist was extremely helpful in coordinating everything. Dr. Shah examined him, applied a plaster, prescribed the necessary medicines, and clearly explained all the precautions and care instructions.
My brother remained in plaster for two months. Yesterday, the plaster was removed, and his ankle bone had healed successfully—without surgery.

I am sharing these experiences after several months because I wanted to describe the complete treatment journey and the final outcomes.

The clinic follows a first-come, first-served system, so waiting times can sometimes be an hour or two. However, I would sincerely advise patients to be patient because you are in very capable hands.

Dr. Kunal Shah has been an angel for us. We are deeply grateful for his care, expertise, and dedication.
Dr. Kunal Shah, thank you for everything. God bless you.

When the annulus is torn, then the nucleus populous (soft interior of disc) extrudes out, protruding through the exterior layer and extending outwards resulting in compression of the adjacent nerve roots and spinal cord within the spinal column, this is called a disc herniation or a slipped disc. Extremely Disappointed with the Doctor’s Approach

I recently visited this doctor for my mother’s severe spine and back issues, hoping for professional and thorough guidance. Unfortunately, our experience was far from satisfactory.

Before the visit, we had proactively conducted basic tests like CBC, ECG, and others to make the process smoother for the doctor. However, during the consultation, he simply glanced at her spine X-ray and suggested getting an MRI done under sedation (since she couldn’t lie down). When I informed him that we had already done tests like CBC, he barely looked at the reports and dismissed them with, “Whichever tests are done, you don’t need to do them again.” This left us questioning the point of getting these tests done if the doctor had no intention of reviewing them properly.

Things got worse when we went to get the MRI done. The anesthesiologist scolded us, asking why the doctor hadn’t checked my mother’s ECG. She has heart issues, which makes anesthesia dangerous due to the risk of BP drops — a potentially fatal situation. As a spine doctor, it was his responsibility to check critical reports like the ECG. That’s why we trust doctors — because as laypersons, we can’t read such reports ourselves!

When I called the doctor to inform him about this oversight, his response was shocking: *“I’m not a physician; I’m a spine doctor. It’s not my job to check that. You should have gone to a physician.”* This level of negligence and passing the buck is unacceptable. Even a general MD doctor can interpret an ECG, and ignoring it could have risked my mother’s life.

Overall, the experience left us feeling frustrated and disappointed. The doctor came across as all talk and no action, showing little regard for patient safety or thoroughness. I wouldn’t recommend him to anyone looking for competent and reliable care.
